summary: Server hangs and game stops responding when loading a chunk containing a structure with an allay
description: When I teleported a few thousand blocks away all chunks stopped loading and using the F3 menu works and gamemode switcher ui and other ui s open up but do nothing. The F3 menu is stuck showing the internal server tick at 18ms and is not allowing chunks to keep loading in. Reloading chunks does not fix this. When the server hangs, commands, etc do not work. Sometimes, 2-8 chunks will load in if you are not inside of the structure that contains allays naturally generated. If you go to save your world while the chunks won t load, you will not be able to save your world and have to force crash the game (No data will be saved if you do this). Summoning an allay using "/summon allay" does not cause this issue. Going to a woodland mansion without any naturally generated allays will not cause this issue. Only structures with naturally generated allays can cause this issue. Code analysis Code analysis by can be found in this comment. Important parts are marked by a star ( ) How to reproduce: 1) Teleport to a far away structure such as woodland mansion, pillager outpost, or any other structure that may contain naturally generated allays 2) Look at the chunks near you, are they loading in? 3a) If they aren t loading in, reload chunks using F3 A, do they load in now? 3b) If they don t load in, you may not have teleported close enough to the woodland mansion, or outpost, try teleporting closer 4a) If they didn t load in now, you have successfully reproduced this bug 4b) If they didn t load in, you are probably on the wrong version of minecraft (Make sure your version is 22w13a, it is likely to have been patched in future snapshots) 5) To exit if this happens; DO NOT USE F3 C AS IT DOES NOT WORK!!! ALT F4 DOES NOT WORK AS WELL!!! (If in the "Saving World" screen) On Windows: Open task manager, and end the task called "OpenJDK Platform binary" On Linux: Open the terminal and kill the OpenJDK process using "kill ", you can use the killall command in the terminal as well, xkill or System Monitor should also be capable On MacOS: In the application press and hold Command Option Shift, press Esc, Confirm force quit (may not ask for confirmation for some apps) "a" and "b" steps are specific to certain conditions and only follow that path if those conditions are met, if new conditions are discovered, comment and I will update the instructions
Steps to Reproduce:
1. Teleport to a far away structure such as woodland mansion, pillager outpost, or any other structure that may contain naturally generated allays.
2. Observe if the chunks near you are loading in.
3. If they aren’t loading in, reload chunks using F3 + A and observe again.
4. If reloading does not load the chunks, teleport closer to the structure.
5. Repeat steps 2-3 until either the chunks load or they do not load at all.
6. If the chunks still do not load after teleporting closer, you have successfully reproduced this bug.
7. Note that commands and UI elements will not work when the server hangs.
8. To exit the game while it is hanging, use task manager on Windows to end the "OpenJDK Platform binary" process, or use terminal commands such as `kill` or `killall` on Linux, or force quit via Command + Option + Shift + Esc on MacOS.
Observed Behavior:
When loading chunks containing structures with naturally generated allays, the server hangs and the game stops responding. This issue occurs when teleporting a few thousand blocks away from the player's initial position, causing all chunk loading to halt. The F3 menu still functions and displays information such as the internal server tick at 18ms, but no chunks are loaded beyond this point. Attempting to reload chunks using the F3 menu does not resolve the issue. Commands and UI elements like the gamemode switcher open but do nothing. Occasionally, 2-8 chunks may load in if you are not inside a structure that contains naturally generated allays. However, saving the world while chunk loading is halted results in an inability to save any changes, necessitating a force crash of the game with no data saved.

Summoning an allay using `/summon allay` does not cause this issue, and neither does visiting a woodland mansion without naturally generated allays. The problem specifically arises only when structures contain naturally generated allays. Code analysis for further details can be found in a specific comment where important parts are marked by a star.

To reproduce the bug:
1. Teleport to a faraway structure such as a woodland mansion, pillager outpost, or any other structure that may contain naturally generated allays.
2. Observe if chunks near you are loading.
3a. If they aren’t loading, attempt reloading chunks using F3 A and check again.
3b. If they still don't load, ensure you have teleported close enough to the woodland mansion or outpost; try teleporting closer.
4a. If chunks still do not load in after these steps, the bug has been successfully reproduced.
4b. If chunks are still not loading, it is possible that you are using an incorrect version of Minecraft (ensure your version is 22w13a as it may have been patched in future snapshots).

To exit if this happens:
- DO NOT USE F3 C AS IT DOES NOT WORK!!!
- ALT F4 DOES NOT WORK AS WELL!!! (If in the "Saving World" screen)
On Windows: Open task manager and end the task called "OpenJDK Platform binary".
On Linux: Use the terminal to kill the OpenJDK process using `kill`, or use commands like `killall`, `xkill`, or System Monitor.
On MacOS: Press and hold Command + Option + Shift, then press Esc and confirm force quit (may not ask for confirmation for some apps).

Steps 3a and 3b are specific to certain conditions; follow that path only if those conditions are met. If new conditions arise, provide feedback for updates.
Expected Behavior: When teleporting near structures containing naturally generated allays, chunks should load normally without any hangs or freezes. The game should remain responsive, allowing commands to work and the F3 menu to update correctly. Chunks should continue to load in as you move around, and saving the world should function properly without needing to force quit the game.
